findings.location: references/framework-execution-models.md, Spring WebFlux, original lines 71–77; final lines 71–85
findings.finding: The property and retained bounds were described, but the affected factory was not explicit. A caller could infer that a separately-created/injected newBoundedElastic scheduler was converted by the shared-scheduler property.
findings.consequence: Incorrect claims of virtual-thread execution on an actual blocking leaf, or an unnecessary model/scheduler replacement.
findings.evidence: Reactor 3.7.2 API distinguishes the global boundedElastic property from newBoundedElastic(int,int,String); the versioned Schedulers source initializes the property in a static final field. The local controlled 3.7.12 experiment confirmed the same distinction.
findings.correction: Named the shared factory, property initialization timing, default-factory newBoundedElastic platform behavior, and bean/factory/override path to subscribeOn/publishOn. Explicitly retained the option to keep an adequate platform-thread isolation boundary.
Added exact Reactor 3.7.2 API/source links near the framework-specific rule and bumped the package patch version.

# Execution model
The startup JVM property makes every boundedElastic scheduler virtual, including JDBC. It also makes blocking safe anywhere inside our reactive pipelines. The existing JDBC admission contract remains required.

This working reactive service has no measured performance or maintainability reason to migrate. No runtime thread capture for a real JDBC invocation is provided. The task is to correct the execution-model ADR, not implement a migration.
